reviewNotes: All 85 saved physical-board states and narration reviewed. Complete five-piece setup: White Kh5/Ba8/b7 versus Black Kh1/Qf4. Four promotion choices are checked at every encoded step: b8=B+/Kg1/Bxf4/Kf1 preserves a White win; b8=Q+/Kg1/Qxf4 is actual stalemate; independently added rook promotion draws and knight promotion loses. The promoted bishop, not Ba8, captures Qf4. After Bxf4 Black has f1 and f2; no two-bishop mate sequence is fabricated. Native image 17 supplies a clear unoccluded root; bases identify squares. Source timings: queen promotion around 20s, bishop promotion around 65s, Kf1 around 81s.
transcript: If the queen is the strongest piece in chess, very clearly, why are we allowed to promote pawns [music] to other pieces? Shouldn't we always want a queen? Well, not exactly. Most of the times that we promote to something that is not a queen is because of something called a stalemate. Take this position, for example. If I now push this pawn and promote to a queen, the white bishop is going to give a check to the black king. But actually, black has a way now to draw this position by moving the king to G1. If the black queen stays on the board, this is going to be a draw. So, white will want to take it. But unfortunately, this is a stalemate, a situation where the king is not in check, but there are no legal moves available. The king is the only piece left, but it cannot move to any of these squares because they're all covered by either the queen or the bishop. So, according to the rules of chess, this position is a draw. So, if we go back to that moment when we promoted the pawn, we will actually find that the only way for white to win this position is to promote the pawn to another bishop. Now, the light-squared bishop still gives a check to the king, so the king has to move. But this time, if it goes to G1, white is free to take the black queen because this time the black king is left with a legal moves. For example, F1. And as long as the black king can move, there is not going to be a stalemate. So, white is going to be using the two bishops to eventually deliver a checkmate.
